subject.title: fix(cron): cap trigger script tool access

question: How should upgrades handle existing trigger-script cron jobs whose creator-derived tool cap was never recorded and cannot be reconstructed?
rationale: Preserving cap-less jobs retains a known privilege-escalation path, while disabling all of them can break legitimate operator-created automation; repository evidence cannot safely choose that tradeoff without owner intent.

options.title: Quarantine Legacy Triggers
options.body: Disable trigger evaluation for cap-less legacy jobs until an operator reviews and re-saves each job with an approved tool policy.

options.title: Accept Forward-Only Hardening
options.body: Merge the current patch and explicitly accept that existing cap-less jobs remain unrestricted until operators audit or edit them.

options.title: Design Provenance First
options.body: Hold the PR until a broader migration or provenance mechanism can classify legacy jobs without stopping all cap-less operator jobs.

recommendation.title: Quarantine Legacy Triggers
recommendation.body: Disable trigger evaluation for cap-less legacy jobs until an operator reviews and re-saves each job with an approved tool policy.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent authorization and cron-runtime history most directly spans the security and compatibility boundary requiring a decision.
